subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback after explicit binding tiers miss, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but changing fallback behavior affects session state, model/provider routing, and permission boundaries, and repository policy treats fallback semantics as a product and security boundary decision.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Keep explicit bindings only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and add clearer docs or doctor/status warnings for Discord accounts that look intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair the fork PR first
options.body: Use the open fork PR as source material only after conflicts, configured-agent guarding, diagnostics, and real Discord proof are addressed.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, tests, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest historical ownership signal for multi-agent routing, shared route resolution, and recent Discord route-helper extraction.
